newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian officials raid activists' offices.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian officials raid activists' offices.

text.p: Officials from Malaysia's Registrar of Companies on Tuesday raided three offices of non-governmental organisations after the government ordered a crackdown on such groups, the national Bernama news agency said.
The officials checked documents, account books and vouchers at the premises of Tenaganita, the Institute of Social Analysis and the Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall in separate raids.
The officers cited a section of the Companies Act empowering them to seize documents if they suspected these would be disposed of in the event of an alleged offence.
The action drew sharp criticism from other non-governmental groups.

"The outrageous action against Tenganita is not only illegal, it has tarnished the image of Malaysia as a civilised and democratic society," Suaram, one of Malaysia's main activist groups, said in a statement.
Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said last weekend that the government was studying ways to bring non-governmental organisations under the control of the Registrar of Societies.
The government would also scrutinise their source of funds, Megat Junid said.

Activist groups in Malaysia have long been the source of a simmering dispute, with the government saying they are largely funded and influenced by overseas human rights and environmentalist organisations.
In November, youth groups allied to the government stormed a conference on East Timor organised by a coalition of local activist groups which had ignored government warnings not to hold the meeting.
Malaysia arrested nearly 60 local activists at the conference and deported some 46 foreign participants.
